meta.tagline: Ouzo, olives and an island in no hurry

overview.title: Welcome to Lesbos
overview.intro: When the ferry docks at Mytilene, what greets you is not a tourist island but a living Greek province. Lesbos is Greece's third-largest island: eleven million olive trees, the world's best ouzo, hot springs, and villages that never surrendered to tourism. Nobody here tries to sell you anything; you sip your coffee, swim, and get pulled into the conversation at the next table. The island is big and unhurried — be unhurried too.

local_word.definition: Greek for 'slowly, slowly': the tempo of Lesbos and its official philosophy. Service running late, ferry delayed? Siga siga. Adopting these two words is the only way to tune into the island.

rules.title: Rent a car — the island is bigger than it looks
rules.description: Lesbos covers 1,600 km²: Mytilene to Molyvos takes over an hour. Buses are sparse; to really see the island you need wheels. The roads are good but winding — no rushing between the olive groves.

rules.title: Never drink ouzo without food
rules.description: Plomari ouzo is the world's finest, but it's drunk the Greek way: always with meze, ice and water. Everyone at the table can spot the tourist who downs the glass in one.

rules.title: Sort your ferry and passport logistics early
rules.description: Coming from Turkey, visa-on-arrival practice and ferry schedules change with the season. Book the Ayvalık–Mytilene crossing ahead and check your return sailing on day one.

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: English in tourist spots, sometimes Turkish

tip.label: The Lesbos philosophy
tip.text: If you notice lunch at a taverna has lasted three hours, don't worry: everything is going exactly right. The island has succeeded in slowing you down.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The key to Lesbos is your own set of wheels; everything else is detail.

items.title: Ferries — Ayvalık and Piraeus
items.description: The Ayvalık–Mytilene crossing runs daily in summer, thinner in winter; about 40 minutes. The big Piraeus ferries are an 8–10 hour overnight voyage. Book ahead and arrive early for passport control.

items.title: Rental car — the island's key
items.description: Offices at the port and airport; reserve ahead in summer. It's the only comfortable way to day-trip to the far ends — Molyvos, Plomari, Sigri. Petrol stations are sparse in the villages; never let the tank drop below half.

items.title: KTEL buses
items.description: A few daily runs from Mytilene to the main towns; cheap but limited. Without a car, build your route around the timetable and never miss the last bus.

items.title: Scooters and ATVs
items.description: Practical for short hops around Mytilene; but the island is windy and the roads twist — a car is safer for the long legs.

items.title: Taxis
items.description: Findable in Mytilene, rare in the villages. Agree the price before long rides; airport to town is short and reasonable.

callout.label: Ferry timing warning
callout.text: If your return is to Ayvalık, check schedule changes on your first day, not your last; sailings get cancelled in strong wind. Plan B is one more night on Lesbos — hardly a punishment.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: There is no single 'centre' on Lesbos; the island splits into four characters. Your choice decides what kind of holiday you get.

local_word.definition: The traditional coffee house on the village square: backgammon, coffee brewed on embers, conversations that last hours. Whichever village you stay in, drink one coffee at the kafeneio — that's where you'll understand the island's rhythm.

items.name: Mytilene — the island capital
items.description: Port, bazaar, restaurants and nightlife are all here. Ideal first and last night if you arrive by ferry; beautiful in its own right with neoclassical mansions and the castle. As a touring base it sits a little far southeast.

items.name: Molyvos (Mithymna) — the northern pearl
items.description: Stone houses, bougainvillea lanes and a Byzantine castle on the hill: the island's postcard. Sunset harbour, an artists' soul and boutique guesthouses make it the corner of Lesbos people fall for. 60 km from Mytilene — and worth it.

items.name: Plomari — the ouzo town
items.description: On the south coast, the capital of the distilleries. Seafront tavernas, a stone-bridged stream and a meze culture taken seriously: the address for a food-and-drink holiday. Agios Isidoros beach is right next door.

items.name: Skala Eresou — the free spirit of the west
items.description: The beach of ancient Eresos, birthplace of the poet Sappho: a long sandy shore, easy-going cafés and a loyal crowd from around the world. One of the island's best sunsets and its most relaxed air.

items.name: Petra and around — for families
items.description: Molyvos's neighbour Petra, with its church on the rock and long shallow beach, is the family classic. Prices softer than Molyvos, the northern routes just as close.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Lesbos lives year-round; the tourist season is short, the beautiful season long.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Flowers and Birds
items.subtitle: Spring · Orchids, flamingos, empty roads
items.description: The island becomes one of Europe's best birdwatching sites: flamingos on the Kalloni salt pans, wild orchids on the hills. Mild air, a still-cool sea, winter prices. The best window for walking and exploring.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: Late May is the island at its greenest: olive groves gleaming, tavernas open, crowds not yet arrived.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Sea Season
items.subtitle: Summer · Warm sea, full tavernas, festivals
items.description: The sea hits 25 degrees, beaches come alive, village festivals (panigiri) follow one another. Even by Greek island standards, Lesbos stays calm in summer — no Mykonos crush here. Around August 15, the Assumption, everything fills up.

callout.label: August note
callout.text: August 15 is the Dormition of the Virgin (Dekapentavgoustos) — Greece's greatest feast after Easter. That week the whole country goes on holiday and thousands of pilgrims come to Agiasos's church of the Virgin; book ferries and rooms ahead.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Harvest Time
items.subtitle: Autumn · Olive harvest, warm sea, golden light
items.description: September is the island's secret peak: warm sea, crowds gone, softened light. In October and November the olive harvest begins; the island returns to its real work and gladly lets guests join in.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: Mid-September the sea is still 23 degrees; the beaches feel nearly private.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Locals' Island
items.subtitle: Winter · Hot springs, kafeneio conversations
items.description: Tourism stops and the island turns inward. The hot springs (Eftalou, Polichnitos) become winter comforts, the ouzo tables move indoors. Most tourist facilities close, but authenticity peaks.

callout.label: Winter tip
callout.text: Slipping into 43-degree water in Eftalou's stone-domed bathhouse while the sea sits at zero is the island's finest winter memory.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The cuisine of Lesbos rests on two pillars: olive oil and the sea. The third arrives at the table with the ouzo.

local_word.definition: The small plates that come with ouzo: not a meal in themselves but fuel for conversation. On Lesbos a meze table lasts hours, and nobody checks the time.

items.name: Kalloni sardines (sardeles pastes)
items.description: The famous sardines of Kalloni Bay are salt-cured for a few hours and served almost raw-fresh; counted among Greece's most celebrated meze. The star of the August sardine festival.

items.name: Plomari ouzo
items.description: The anise national drink finds its finest form on this island; the distilleries of Plomari and Mytilene export it to the world. It clouds over ice, opens with meze, ends in conversation.

items.name: Ladotyri — cheese aged in olive oil
items.description: The island's protected sheep's cheese matures in jars of olive oil; hard, salty, full of character. Grilled as saganaki it becomes a feast of its own.
items.tag: PDO product · try it as saganaki

items.name: Olives and olive oil
items.description: On an island of eleven million trees, the oil is fresh enough to drink. Buy a bottle of cold-pressed from a village market; it will be the most precious gift in your suitcase.

items.name: Grilled octopus and calamari
items.description: The octopus drying in the sun outside the harbour tavernas is the evening's menu: char-grilled, with lemon, by the water. Molyvos and Skala Sikamnias harbours are the classic addresses.

items.name: Baklava and amygdalota
items.description: The Ottoman-heritage sweet tradition is alive and well: pistachio baklava, almond amygdalota and kadayif with ice cream. The patisseries of Mytilene's bazaar are a century old.

callout.label: The taverna rule
callout.text: Skip the place with a laminated photo menu; trust the taverna that recites the day's fish out loud. 'Ti fresko ehete?' (What's fresh today?) opens every door.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: The best places on Lesbos are unsigned; for these six you no longer need a local's tip-off.

items.name: Sigri Petrified Forest
items.description: At the island's western tip, sequoia trunks sealed in volcanic ash 20 million years ago: a UNESCO geopark, an open-air museum and a landscape like the moon. Few places on Earth compare.

items.name: Skala Sikamnias
items.description: The north coast's tiny fishing harbour: the Panagia Gorgona chapel on its rock, tavernas shaded by a mulberry tree, and the atmosphere the writer Stratis Myrivilis carried into literature. Island calm, distilled.

items.rarity: A hot spring at the sea's edge
items.name: Eftalou Hot Springs
items.description: Near Molyvos, an Ottoman-era stone-domed bathhouse above a pebble beach: healing water at 43 degrees, the cool Aegean two steps away. The hot-cold ritual costs a symbolic entrance fee.

items.rarity: A Byzantine monastery on the hill
items.name: Moni Limonos
items.description: The island's largest monastery: peacocks in the courtyard, manuscripts in the library, centuries in the silence. Just off the Kalloni road, a world most visitors never turn into.

items.name: Kalloni Salt Pans
items.description: Thousands of flamingos and over 250 bird species in spring and autumn: one of Europe's finest birdwatching sites. Bring binoculars, take a hide, wait.

items.name: Agiasos
items.description: A mountain village in the chestnut forest on the slopes of Mount Olympos: ceramic workshops, a centuries-old church of the Virgin, cool stone lanes. The island's freshest escape in high summer.

callout.label: Western tip bonus
callout.text: If you've made it to Sigri, end the day at Gavathas beach: hard to find on tourist maps, with a sunset no map could hold.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Lesbos is poor in traps — no tourist industry was ever built, so no games were either. Still, know these four.

items.name: Leaving the ferry ticket to the last day
items.description: The Ayvalık line fills up in summer and cancels in wind; hearing 'no seats tomorrow' at the counter is the classic end to a holiday.
items.instead: Buy the round trip up front and confirm the time a day before returning; stay flexible — the island deserves an extra night anyway.

items.name: The 'I'll see the island in a day' plan
items.description: Small on the map, the island is a real journey on the ground; attempting Molyvos + Plomari + Sigri in one day is a holiday spent at the wheel.
items.instead: Split the island into regions: one day north (Molyvos–Petra), one day south (Plomari–Agiasos), one day west (Kalloni–Sigri).

items.name: Tourist ouzo from the supermarket shelf
items.description: The fancy bottles at the airport and gift shops are usually the island's ordinary line; you're paying for packaging.
items.instead: Buy ouzo from a distillery's own shop or a village grocer; tasting and choosing in Plomari is half the fun.

items.name: Anchoring at a single beach
items.description: Staying at the hotel beach because it's easy means missing the island's coastal variety: every cove has a different character.
items.instead: Try a new cove daily: the clarity of Agios Isidoros, the sand of Skala Eresou, the red pebbles of Tsonia — the car is already rented.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: Telling whether a place is touristy on Lesbos is easy: how many languages is the menu in? Greek only and handwritten means you're sitting on a gold mine.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: Mytilene + the postcard of the north

steps.title: Mytilene bazaar and castle
steps.description: Walk the Ermou street bazaar, look over the harbour from the Byzantine-Ottoman castle walls; coffee at an old bazaar kafeneio.

steps.title: North road — Kalloni stop
steps.description: Head for Molyvos; break early at a bay taverna in Kalloni for sardines + ouzo. In season, spot the flamingos on the salt pans.

steps.title: The lanes of Molyvos
steps.description: Climb between stone mansions to the castle: whitewash, bougainvillea and the gulf below. The island's most beautiful half hour is this slope.

steps.title: Hot spring + sea at Eftalou
steps.description: Warm up in the bathhouse's 43 degrees, dive into the Aegean two steps away; repeat. Island therapy in summary.

steps.title: Sunset at Molyvos harbour
steps.description: Grilled octopus at a harbour taverna, ouzo on ice and the sinking sun; whoever hurries, loses.

steps.title: Return or stay
steps.description: The night road back to Mytilene takes an hour; the wise traveller booked a room in Molyvos.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the island as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: Mytilene and the north
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: bazaar, Kalloni, Molyvos, Eftalou.

steps.title: A taste of the south
steps.description: Agiasos's chestnut-shaded lanes and ceramic workshops in the morning, a distillery tour + tasting in Plomari at noon, the sea at Agios Isidoros in the afternoon, a meze table on the Plomari waterfront at night.

steps.title: The wild west
steps.description: Set out early: the Sigri Petrified Forest museum and grounds, fish at Sigri harbour at noon, the sea and sunset at Skala Eresou — farewell on Sappho's beach.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Even three words of Greek start the free treats coming at a taverna; arriving from the neighbouring shore doubles the effect.

items.meaning: Hello / goodbye — the formal, safe greeting
Thank you — looks hard, lands by the second try
Please / you're welcome — Greek's joker card
Cheers! — ouzo glasses rise to this
Slowly, slowly — the island's rhythm; say it once and you're a local
